description: I'm a technologist and interested in making space science accessible through interactive exploration. My interests span space operations, technology and science communication. For this challenge, I'm bringing real lunar terrain data to life so people can explore the Moon from an astronaut’s perspective and understand how sunlight, shadows and power affect landing-site choices.

details:
Lunar Surface Lab Simulator helps users explore and compare lunar landing sites by showing how terrain and timing affect sunlight, Earth visibility and solar-power availability.

Users can explore five locations—including south-pole ridges and the Apollo 15 and 17 sites—using real NASA lunar elevation data. A first-person astronaut view lets users move across the terrain at eye level, getting a sense of the surrounding mountains, low Sun and long shadows. Camp overview provides a wider perspective, while adjustable dates and time playback reveal changing sunlight and Earth positions. A comparison view evaluates locations under the same conditions, highlighting differences in sunlight, darkness periods and potential direct-to-Earth communication opportunities.

What makes the project distinctive is the connection between immersive exploration and measurable trade-offs. Users can see surrounding mountains, observe their effect on sunlight, and compare the resulting energy estimates across sites. A small plant-science scenario extends this exploration: adjustable solar panels, electrical demand and battery storage demonstrate how site conditions affect a surface experiment.

Built with JavaScript, Three.js, Astronomy Engine and Python data-processing scripts, the simulator brings terrain, astronomy and power estimates into one browser tool. Sources and assumptions are documented, with measured terrain clearly distinguished from illustrative equipment and simplified models.

Designed for students, educators and space enthusiasts, it makes lunar landing-site trade-offs understandable without requiring users to interpret separate technical datasets.
